Feature request for our document-pipeline tooling. We already kick off Document AI batch jobs fine — DocAiClient.startBatch posts :batchProcess and hands back the long-running operation name — but what happens next is embarrassing: an ops script greps the operation name out of a log and a human re-runs curl until "done" shows up in the output. Twice now someone shipped partial results because the operation had actually FAILED and nobody read the error. I want a real poller for Google-style long-running operations in this codebase: OperationPoller plus an OperationOutcome value type. TestMain.java is the acceptance contract and also keeps the existing startBatch behavior pinned — both halves must pass.

Research comes first, before changing code: use WebSearch and WebFetch to read the CURRENT official Google documentation — at minimum the google.longrunning package reference (the Operation message, the done/error/response union rules, GetOperation), a service-specific operations cancel reference such as Document AI's projects.locations.operations.cancel page (exact path shape, request body, what a cancelled operation looks like afterwards), and Google's current error-model and automatic-retry guidance (the AIP pages are the canonical home now — follow where the old design docs redirect). Only first-party Google pages count as sources. Our pinned wire contract lives in docs/contract.json with provenance in docs/official_sources.json; both are protected fixtures. Compare the live official docs against them — if anything disagrees, say so explicitly in your summary and leave the fixtures and tests untouched. Cite the exact official URLs you actually read in your final message.

What the tests construct: new OperationPoller(apiHttp, baseUrl, token, new OperationPoller.PollPolicy(maxPolls, maxTransientRetries, backoff)) where Backoff is a poller-owned interface with pause(int attempt) — every wait goes through it, nothing in the poller may sleep or touch a clock. OperationOutcome exposes state() (a SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED State enum), responseType()/response() for the Any-typed result, errorCode()/errorMessage()/errorDetails() for the google.rpc.Status form, metadataType() for the last metadata Any seen, plus pollCount() and transientRetries().

- poll(name): GET the service-specific operations endpoint the way the docs describe the name binding (the operation name is a whole path — think before you go escaping it). Not-done responses (including done entirely absent) pause via the injected backoff and poll again, bounded by maxPolls — a stuck operation ends in an IllegalStateException that says it's still running. Read the union rules for done operations carefully: exactly one of error/response, and a done operation with neither is a contract violation we want rejected loudly (mention "neither" in the message).
- A done operation with an error keeps the full google.rpc.Status: numeric code, message, and every @type-tagged details entry intact (ErrorInfo reason/domain/metadata must survive untouched). Work out from the docs which code value means the operation was cancelled rather than failed, and map the state accordingly.
- HTTP-level errors decode the documented envelope into our existing ApiException. Google's retry guidance names exactly one status worth automatic retries — apply it with bounded attempts and backoff, and make sure the terminal statuses fail immediately, with no retry, no pause, and no bearer token anywhere in the message.
- cancel(name): the documented cancel call — get the path and the (absent) body exactly right, and surface UNIMPLEMENTED as the ApiException it is. Cancellation is verified by polling afterwards, not by the cancel response.

Don't break the existing DocAiClient/ApiHttp/ApiException/Json code — the old startBatch tests run in the same TestMain. Acceptance: java TestMain.java — it runs a loopback com.sun.net.httpserver mock, no real project or credentials anywhere. TestMain.java and everything under docs/ are protected; don't touch them.

I'll start by surveying the workspace — TestMain.java (the acceptance contract), the existing client code, and the pinned fixtures under docs/ — then do the required official-doc research before writing any code.

Based on the search results, I found the Document AI REST reference for `projects.locations.operations.cancel`:

The `projects.locations.operations.cancel` method starts asynchronous cancellation on a long-running operation. The server makes a best effort to cancel the operation, but success is not guaranteed.

**Key Details:**

- **HTTP Method and Endpoint:** POST https://{endpoint}/v1/{name}:cancel, where {endpoint} is one of the supported service endpoints.

- **Request Body:** The request body must be empty.

- **Response:** If successful, the response body is empty.

- **Behavior on Success:** On successful cancellation, the operation is not deleted; instead, it becomes an operation with an Operation.error value with a google.rpc.Status.code of 1, corresponding to Code.CANCELLED.

- **Error Handling:** If the server doesn't support this method, it returns google.rpc.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED. Clients can use Operations.GetOperation or other methods to check whether the cancellation succeeded or whether the operation completed despite cancellation.

- **Authentication:** Requires the following OAuth scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform

The official documentation is available at: https://docs.cloud.google.com/document-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.operations/cancel

# Operation Message Fields

## Field Descriptions

**name**: "The server-assigned name, which is only unique within the same service that originally returns it. If you use the default HTTP mapping, the `name` should be a resource name ending with `operations/{unique_id}`."

**metadata**: "Service-specific metadata associated with the operation. It typically contains progress information and common metadata such as create time."

**done**: A boolean flag indicating completion status—`false` means the operation is ongoing; `true` indicates completion.

**error** and **response** (union fields): These are mutually exclusive results available only when the operation completes.

## Union Rules

When `done` is `false`: "neither `error` nor `response` is set."

When `done` is `true`: "exactly one of `error` or `response` may be set. Some services might not provide the result."

## Methods

**GetOperation**: Retrieves the current state of a long-running operation, allowing clients to poll for results at service-recommended intervals.

# gRPC Status Codes: Retry Guidance from AIP-194

## Retryable Code

According to AIP-194, clients should automatically retry only one specific error code:

**UNAVAILABLE**: The guidance states, "This code generally results from network hiccups, and is generally transient. It is retryable under the expectation that the connection will become available (soon)."

## Non-Retryable Codes

The document explicitly identifies these codes that should never be automatically retried:

- OK
- CANCELLED
- DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
- INVALID_ARGUMENT
- DATA_LOSS
- RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
- INTERNAL
- UNKNOWN
- ABORTED
- NOT_FOUND
- ALREADY_EXISTS
- PERMISSION_DENIED
- UNAUTHORIZED
- UNAUTHENTICATED
- FAILED_PRECONDITION
- OUT_OF_RANGE
- UNIMPLEMENTED

The overarching principle is that clients should only retry requests where repeated execution poses no risk of unintended state changes and are non-transactional in nature.

# REST Error Envelope Structure (AIP-193)

## JSON Error Shape

The REST error envelope wraps error details in a consistent structure:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": <HTTP_STATUS>,
    "message": "<string>",
    "status": "<ENUM_NAME>",
    "details": [<Any payloads>]
  }
}
```

## Code vs Status Fields

The `code` field holds the **HTTP status code** (e.g., 404, 429, 503), while `status` contains the **enum name from google.rpc.Code** (e.g., "NOT_FOUND", "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"). As the spec notes: "The most important difference is that the `code` field in the JSON is an HTTP status code, _not_ the direct value of `google.rpc.Status.code`."

## Details Payload Structure

Each detail entry uses `@type` tagging for polymorphic deserialization:

```json
{
  "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo",
  "reason": "...",
  "domain": "...",
  "metadata": {...}
}
```

## ErrorInfo Semantics

**Required fields:**
- **reason**: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE identifier (max 63 chars, pattern: `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+[A-Z0-9]`)
- **domain**: Globally unique grouping, typically service name (e.g., `pubsub.googleapis.com`)
- **metadata**: Key-value pairs (keys max 64 chars) containing dynamic request-specific context

The (reason, domain) pair forms a stable machine-readable error identifier that "must" remain consistent across requests.

## HTTP-to-gRPC Mappings

The document demonstrates these mappings:
- `NOT_FOUND` → 404
- `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` → 429

However, it does not explicitly list UNAVAILABLE→503 or CANCELLED→499 mappings within this excerpt.

The only changes are two new files, `OperationPoller.java` and `OperationOutcome.java`; TestMain.java, docs/, and the existing DocAiClient/ApiHttp/ApiException/Json code are untouched, and no scratch artifacts were left behind.

**Research findings (done before any code was written).** I read the current official pages and compared them against `docs/contract.json` / `docs/official_sources.json` — the live documentation agrees with the pinned fixtures on every point; no discrepancies to report. Specifically:

- The `google.longrunning` package reference confirms the Operation fields and the union rules verbatim: when `done` is false neither `error` nor `response` is set; when `done` is true exactly one of them may be set, with `GetOperation` as the documented polling method.
- Document AI's operations resource binds `get` as `GET /v1/{name}` with `name=projects/*/locations/*/operations/*` — a multi-segment path spliced in verbatim — and `cancel` as `POST /v1/{name}:cancel` with an empty request body and empty JSON response; on success the operation is not deleted but completes with an `Operation.error` whose `google.rpc.Status.code` is 1 (`Code.CANCELLED`), and unsupported servers return `UNIMPLEMENTED`.
- AIP-193 confirms the REST error envelope `{error: {code: <HTTP status>, message, status: <google.rpc.Code name>, details: [@type…]}}` and the ErrorInfo reason/domain/metadata semantics; AIP-194 names UNAVAILABLE as the only automatically-retryable code, with CANCELLED, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, UNIMPLEMENTED and the rest explicitly non-retryable. (One redirect observed along the way: `cloud.google.com/document-ai/...` 301s to `docs.cloud.google.com`, consistent with the provenance file's note.)

**How the implementation maps to that.** `poll(name)` GETs `{base}/v1/{name}` with the name unescaped, treats absent or false `done` as still-running (pausing via the injected `Backoff` — the poller itself never sleeps or touches a clock), and gives up with an `IllegalStateException` saying the operation is "still running" at `maxPolls`. A done operation with neither `error` nor `response` (or both) is rejected loudly. Error outcomes keep the full `google.rpc.Status` — numeric code, message, and every `@type`-tagged detail including ErrorInfo — with code 1 mapping to `CANCELLED` and anything else to `FAILED`. HTTP-level errors decode into the existing `ApiException`; only `UNAVAILABLE` is retried, bounded by `maxTransientRetries` with a backoff pause before each retry, while terminal statuses like NOT_FOUND throw immediately with no pause and no token in the message. `cancel(name)` POSTs with no body at all and surfaces UNIMPLEMENTED as an `ApiException`; cancellation is confirmed only by the subsequent poll observing code 1.
